passage: I am Tushar and my desk is behind Radhika's, so I heard it. Before maths, Ramesh leaned over and whispered, "Show me your answers, just this once?" Radhika kept her page flat. "No, Ramesh. But I will go through the steps with you after class if you like." Ramesh rolled his eyes and turned away. I thought that was the end of their friendship. But at the bell Radhika waited beside his desk with her notebook, and they went to the corridor bench, where she drew out the steps of long division. Ramesh was frowning, but he was writing. I cannot know if he was still annoyed. When the next bell rang he said, "Okay, one more."

qa.q: What did Radhika offer to do instead of showing her answers?
qa.a: She offered to go through the steps with Ramesh after class.

qa.q: What might Ramesh have felt when Radhika said no?
qa.a: Annoyed and embarrassed, since he rolled his eyes and turned away, though Tushar cannot be sure.

qa.q: What could Radhika do if Ramesh keeps asking for answers?
qa.a: Repeat the offer to study together, because she can hold firm without ending the friendship.

qa.q: How might Radhika see Ramesh's request to copy?
qa.a: Radhika will not show her answers, but she still wants to help, so she offers to go through the steps with him after class.

grounding: A friend asks to copy the maths answers, and the girl says no while offering to explain the method after class.

passage:
Monday: Before maths, Deepika slid her notebook towards Preeti. "Just let me copy questions four to eight. Please. I didn't get fractions at all." Preeti's stomach tightened. "No. But I'll show you how after class. Promise." Deepika sulked and turned away.
Tuesday: Deepika didn't sit with her at lunch. Preeti felt terrible but didn't change her answer. After the last bell she waited by the gate with her notebook anyway. Deepika came, arms crossed. "Fine. Show me." They sat on the steps for twenty minutes.
Friday: In the class test, Deepika finished the fractions section and grinned across the room. At lunch she sat next to Preeti again and split her samosa without a word.

qa.q: Which questions did Deepika want to copy?
How did Preeti feel on Tuesday?
qa.a: Terrible when Deepika didn't sit with her, but still firm in her answer.

qa.q: What else could Preeti have said on Monday?
qa.a: She could also have told Deepika she was worried about her, to show the no was not about the friendship.

qa.q: How does Deepika's attitude change over the week?
qa.a: From sulking to accepting help, then grinning in the test and sharing her samosa.

grounding: Over a week, a girl refuses to let a friend copy, offers to explain the method instead, and keeps the friendship.

passage: Nitin, your friend wants to copy your homework? Let me tell you what I did when I was a girl of eleven. My best friend Rukhsana leaned over one morning and said, "Sabina, give me your arithmetic book for five minutes. Just the answers." I wanted to say yes. She was my best friend. But I also knew she would get the same sums in the exam, and my book wouldn't be sitting next to her then. So I said, "No. But come to my house after school, and I'll show you how to do them." She didn't talk to me all through recess. That evening she came anyway, with a guava in each hand. We sat on the steps till dark. And we stayed friends for sixty years.

qa.q: What did Rukhsana bring that evening?
How did young Sabina feel when Rukhsana asked?
qa.a: Torn and tempted, wanting to say yes to her best friend.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story mattered most?
qa.a: Saying no but offering to teach after school, which helped Rukhsana without breaking the rule.

qa.q: How might Rukhsana have felt during recess?
qa.a: Hurt or annoyed, not talking to Sabina, before choosing to come that evening anyway.

grounding: An elder recalls refusing to let a friend copy, offering to explain the sums instead, and keeping the friendship.
